dossier.mechanism: Pawza turns the paper the vet hands you into a private, structured record on the iPhone or iPad itself. You photograph a certificate, lab result, prescription label or discharge note. Apple's Vision OCR reads it on the device, and on iOS 26+ with Apple Intelligence an on-device model fills in vaccine, date given, due date, medication, dose, vet and clinic. You confirm each field before anything is saved. Every due date becomes one gentle local reminder, and the whole history goes back out as a one-tap vet-visit PDF (Pro). There is no Pawza server and no account, so the scan works in airplane mode.
dossier.audienceScene: A dog or cat owner, often with more than one pet. One moment is the kitchen table the evening after a vet visit, holding a creased vaccination certificate and a prescription label. Another is the kennel or groomer counter, being asked for proof of Bordetella. Most arrive on a phone from Google ('pet vaccination tracker app', 'dog vaccine record app'), from an AI answer, or from a comparison search ('11pets alternative', 'PetDesk alternative'). Desktop visitors still have to get the app onto their iPhone, hence the QR.
dossier.culturalHome: Household pet paperwork and the vet visit: the vaccination booklet with peel-off vial stickers, a clinic stamp and ballpoint dates; the label on the pill vial; the kennel's proof-of-vaccination check; the expanding file or kitchen drawer of vet invoices; the microchip number; collar tags; the daily walk. Owners name their pets like family and photograph them constantly. The developer's journal frames vet paperwork as a household document ('it names you before it names the dog') and calls airplane mode the honest test.
dossier.mustProve: Four things in one viewport. Paper becomes a record: a vet document read into typed fields you confirm, which is the app's own line 'Snap it. Pawza files it.' It happens on the device with no account. It costs 'Free — Pawza Pro from $2.99/mo' and is free for one pet. And the working App Store badge is there, plus the QR on desktop. Warmth for the pet comes from the real records and the dog and cat in the screenshots, not from cartoon paws.
dossier.categoryDefault: A pastel teal-and-orange pet-app landing page: a smiling retriever photo or cartoon dog, a floating phone mockup at right, paw-print confetti, rounded bubbly sans (Nunito/Quicksand), a 'Your pet's health in one place' headline over a badge row, three paw-icon feature cards, star testimonials and three pricing cards.
dossier.predictableOpposite: The clinical EHR: white and hospital blue, shields and padlocks, 'bank-grade security', sterile tables. Or the heirloom route: cream paper, serif and italic 'family album' in lamplight. That second one is also the app's own UI (cream #EEE9DB, caramel #C28E57, serif titles), and it is the spent rendition prior.
dossier.literalReading: Pawza reads as paw: paw prints, pawprint trails, paw stamps. Only candidate #7 uses it, and it treats the paw as track-reading (field-guide prints in fresh snow), not as a sticker.

_data/transparency.yml (pawza): tracking false, 0 tracking domains, third_party_sdks 1 (ZIPFoundation, local archive handling, no network), no account. Network calls: none (optional CloudKit private DB). Analytics: none. Required Reason APIs: 2 (UserDefaults CA92.1, File Timestamp C617.1). Permissions: Camera, Photo Library, Local notifications. The incumbent '0 third-party SDKs' trust fact is therefore NOT true for Pawza.

candidates.name: The vaccination booklet: peel-off vial labels, a clinic stamp, ballpoint dates
candidates.why: Every owner has one, and it is exactly the paper Pawza is built to read: a ruled grid of vaccine · batch · date given · valid until · vet, filled with stickers, a violet stamp and ballpoint. It carries the mechanism directly. The same grid shown 'as written' and then 'as read' is the scan, the 'valid until' column is the reminder, and the clean reissued page is the vet PDF.

candidates.name: Collar tags on the split ring (ID, rabies and licence tags)
candidates.why: Every dog owner handles them daily, and the rabies tag is renewed with each booster. It carries the mechanism as a record condensed to what fits on a tag: name, chip number, rabies year, clinic. Each new record adds a tag to the ring, and the year stamped on it is the due date. It is weaker on scanning and on cats.

candidates.name: The pharmacy dispensing label on the amber pill vial
candidates.why: Anyone giving monthly Apoquel or heartworm tablets reads one daily, and how_it_works names the prescription label as a scan source. It carries the mechanism as labels: dose, frequency, 'refills: 2', 'discard after' and prescriber are the very fields Pawza extracts, and the refill and discard dates become reminders. It is narrow on vaccines and history.

candidates.name: The household expanding file (13-pocket accordion folder), 'the drawer of paper in your kitchen'
candidates.why: It is the developer's own image (the journal's kitchen drawer of vet paper) and the app's own verb ('Snap it. Pawza files it.'). It carries the mechanism as filing. Loose paper enters the front pocket, is read, and drops behind the right tab. The tabs are the record's categories and the page's navigation. The file never leaves the house, which is on-device.

candidates.name: The handheld microchip reader and its LCD readout
candidates.why: Owners have watched the vet or shelter wave it over the shoulders, and the screenshots show a 15-digit chip number. It carries the mechanism as local reading: the reader reads the chip with no network and shows the result on its own screen, just as Pawza reads a page on the device. It is thin on reminders, history and warmth.

candidates.name: Pet-food bag panels: guaranteed analysis and the feeding guide
candidates.why: Owners read it at the scoop every day. It carries the 'privacy shown, not claimed' leg as an ingredient panel of the app (tracking domains 0, ad and analytics SDKs 0, local libraries 1, network calls none, from transparency.yml) and the plans as a feeding-guide table. It barely carries scanning.

candidates.name: Literal reading: paw prints read as tracks (field-guide track plates and a dog's first trail in fresh snow)
candidates.why: This is the name's literal reading, so it ranks last. Taken as track-reading rather than as a sticker, it carries the mechanism as a trail. Each print is a dated record, the dashed prints ahead are reminders, and the open snow that nothing crossed is the privacy story ('No tracking of you'). Dog prints show claws and cat prints don't, so two crossing trails are the multi-pet household.

styles.label: Thirteen-Pocket File
styles.lineage: The household 13-pocket expanding file in translucent blue polypropylene, sold in every supermarket stationery aisle: a fan of staggered index tabs with white insert labels, a front label panel and an elastic closure. It joins two sources: the developer's journal image of 'the drawer of paper in your kitchen', and the app's own value point 'Snap it. Pawza files it.' The journal's twelve record categories supply the index.
styles.thesis: The page is the pet's expanding file. Loose vet paper goes into the front pocket, Pawza reads it and files it behind the right tab, the index tabs are the navigation, and every section is a pocket whose heading tab steps across the page like real cut tabs. It refuses the split-hero phone mockup and the pastel paw-print landing page.
styles.scene: A Sunday afternoon at the kitchen table the day after a vet visit: an owner with a creased certificate, a receipt and a prescription label beside a blue plastic expanding file, in flat window daylight. That makes the scheme light: white paper is the reading surface, and the saturated plastic is an object colour, not darkness.

styles.navigation: The index tabs are the nav. The top row holds seven anchor tabs. After the hero it condenses into a sticky 44px row, and the current pocket's tab rises 6px and gets a 3px #FFD23F top edge (IntersectionObserver; static without JS). On mobile, 'Tabs' is a <details> that lists all 13 pockets as stacked white insert labels, plus Privacy policy and Support. Inside the page, each pocket's H2 sits in its own tab on the pocket's top edge. Scrolling goes front-to-back through the file, every pocket at the same scale, and each pocket's tab moves one slot right (6 slots on desktop, 3 on mobile), so the headings descend the page as a real cut-tab cascade. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'File it'. In the Scanning pocket, a sample certificate is set in HTML with the field values from screenshot 2 (Vaccination certificate · 15 May 2026 · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital · 41.2 kg · next visit due 15 May 2027) and labelled 'Sample document — values from Pawza's App Store screenshots'. A real <button> 'Snap it' starts the sequence. A 2px #FFD23F read-line sweeps the sheet top to bottom (900ms, transform only), and each field it passes gains a yellow underline. A typed white slip then slides out from behind the sheet, listing Title, Date, Veterinarian, Clinic, Weight and Next visit due, each with a real 'Confirm' checkbox (step 4: nothing is saved until you confirm). Once all are ticked, the slip slides down behind the Records tab and 'Reminder set before 15 May 2027' appears under the Reminders tab. Without JS, the certificate and the filled slip render side by side, the checkboxes are plain inputs, and the steps text explains the flow. With reduced motion there is no sweep and nothing slides: 'Snap it' swaps to the filled slip instantly, and a static 'Filed under Records' line replaces the drop.
styles.motionGrammar: Pocket physics. Paper only moves vertically, in and out of pockets (translateY, 220–280ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)). Tabs lift 4–6px on hover and when current. There are no fades, no parallax and no entrance cascades: sections are simply there. The strap slides up in 180ms. With reduced motion, every movement becomes an instant state change.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are each a single sheet pulled from the file. Above the sheet is a 120px cobalt band holding the tab row, with a front tab 'Pawza' linking back to /apps/pawza/ and the page's own tab lifted ('Privacy policy', 'Support', 'Pawza vs PetDesk'). The reading column is one white sheet: 68ch, Sofia Sans 400 18/1.6 #14161C, H1 in SSEC 800 56px, H2s in SSEC 700 30px. Tables are filing tables with 1px rules. The alternatives verdict becomes two typed lists, 'Choose Pawza if' and 'Choose PetDesk if'. FAQs are <details>. Support is a contact sheet: the email as one large typed line, and what to include as a checklist. Every page ends with the elastic strap and the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. The plastic, tabs, labels, strap and sample certificate are CSS/HTML. It uses the existing icon, screenshots 1–8, assets/qr/pawza.svg and the Apple badge.
styles.risk: The world reads as admin: it sells order more than love, so the dog and cat photos in the screenshots and the hero copy have to carry the warmth. A saturated blue ground across 14 sections can tire the eye, so every long text must sit on white paper. The tab cascade must keep headings scannable (3 slots on mobile). The sample certificate must never look like a real clinic's document.
styles.memoryTest: The pet app whose site was a blue plastic accordion file. The tabs were the menu, and I watched a vet certificate get read, confirmed and dropped behind the Records tab.

styles.label: The Vaccination Booklet
styles.lineage: The pet vaccination booklet and the vaccination pages of pet-passport-style booklets: a pocket-sized stapled booklet with a ruled grid per page (vaccine and manufacturer · batch no. · date given · valid from · valid until · veterinarian). The vet sticks in the peel-off label from the vaccine vial, presses the clinic's rubber stamp in violet ink and writes the dates in ballpoint. Field labels are printed in several languages because the booklet travels. Generic booklet only: no government emblem, no blue EU cover, no official wording.
styles.thesis: The page is the booklet Pawza reads. Each spread is a ruled record page where the vet's stickers, stamp and ballpoint are the 'as written' layer and Pawza's typed fields are the 'as read' layer in the same grid, so the scan is shown in the paper the visitor already owns. It refuses the pet-app phone mockup and the clinical white EHR.
styles.scene: The front desk of a boarding kennel under flat ceiling fluorescents: the owner flips through the dog's dog-eared booklet because the kennel wants proof of Bordetella. That makes the scheme light: cool, even light on pale green security-tint pages.

styles.navigation: The running head is the nav: a 48px cover-green bar, sticky after the hero, with 'Pawza' at left and anchors at right (Vaccinations · How it reads · Treatments · For the vet · Privacy · Fees · Questions). The current spread's link gets a 2px #F3E26B underline. 'Contents' opens a <details> set like the booklet's contents page, listing each section with its folio range. Every spread carries running heads (left 'Pawza · Pet health record', right the section title) and folios at its outer corners. Mobile shows 'Contents' only. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'As written ⇄ As read'. A two-state switch (two real radio inputs styled as paper tabs) sits above the vaccination grid. 'As written' shows the vet's layer: stickers, ballpoint dates and the violet stamp. 'As read' shows Pawza's layer: in every cell a typed value in Encode Sans 600 replaces the ballpoint (Rabies · 7 May 2026 · 7 May 2027 · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital), each followed by a small violet 'confirmed' tick, and the highlighter becomes the line 'Reminder before 4 Nov 2026'. It is pure CSS (:has() on the radio state): cells cross-dissolve over 160ms, staggered 40ms per row in reading order. Both layers are always in the DOM, and the typed values are the accessible text. Without JS it works unchanged; where :has() is unsupported, the two layers stack in each cell, ballpoint above and typed below. With reduced motion the swap is instant, with no stagger, and the highlighter is static.
styles.motionGrammar: Ink, not paper. Nothing slides, flips or turns pages. The only motion is ink changing state: 160ms cross-dissolves in reading order, the highlighter drawing left to right once (320ms) when the grid first enters view, and the sticky strip sliding up in 180ms. Stamps never 'slam'. With reduced motion, everything is static.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are single booklet pages. A cover-green frame (24px on desktop, 8px on mobile) and a running head ('Pawza · Privacy policy · Datenschutz · Confidentialité') carry the world. The reading column sits on plain #E8EFE6 with no guilloche behind the text: 66ch, Encode Sans 400 18/1.6 #17201B (14:1). H1 is Expanded 800 40px and H2s Expanded 700 24px. Comparison tables are ruled booklet grids with Condensed 600 heads. The 'Honest verdict' pair becomes two ruled columns, 'Choose Pawza if' and 'Choose 11pets if'. FAQs are <details>. Support is a 'Notes' page: the email as a typed line in Expanded 700 24px, and what to include as a ruled checklist. Each page closes with the Get Pawza box.
styles.assetsNeeded: One small guilloche tile, a hand-drawn SVG line pattern of about 2 KB, as a production task. Until it exists, a plain #E8EFE6 page with #CFDDCF ruling works. Stickers, stamps and ballpoint are HTML/CSS plus Reenie Beanie. Everything else exists: icon, screenshots, QR, badge.
styles.risk: This is the familiar route. The booklet is the category's own document, which is why it ranks #1 and also why it is the safe pick: document-as-page is a known editorial move. Overdone, it reads as a government form, so the multilingual labels and stamps must stay sparse. Handwriting fonts look fake at scale, so it stays on dates. It must not resemble the EU pet passport (no emblem, no blue cover, no 'European Union'), and screenshot 7's real vaccine brand must not reach the stickers.
styles.memoryTest: The site was the dog's vaccination booklet: stickers, a violet vet stamp, ballpoint dates. One switch turned the scrawl into typed Pawza records.

styles.label: Fresh Snow Trail
styles.lineage: Animal-track field guides: Olaus J. Murie's A Field Guide to Animal Tracks (Peterson series, 1954) and Mark Elbroch's Mammal Tracks & Sign (2003). They supply life-size print plates, gait diagrams, and the dog-versus-cat rule (dogs register claw marks; cats walk with claws retracted). These meet the owner's own winter ritual: the dog's first trail across fresh snow. It is the literal reading of the name (paw), taken as reading evidence rather than as a sticker.
styles.thesis: The page is one dog's trail across fresh snow. Every print is a dated record, the dashed prints ahead are reminders, and the open snow where nothing walked is the privacy story: every track your pet makes is kept, and nothing tracks you. It refuses the category's cartoon paw-print confetti by turning the paw into field-guide evidence.
styles.scene: The first walk of a January morning after overnight snow in the park: an owner in gloves, lead in one hand and phone in the other, a low white sun throwing blue shadows into the dog's fresh prints. That makes the scheme light: cold, high-key white.

type.rationale: Albert Sans (Usted, 2021) is a geometric grotesk in the Scandinavian-modernist vein. Its open apertures stay crisp in cold, high-key light, and at 800 it is dense enough to hold a white field the way the dark prints do. One family keeps the snowfield quiet, so the prints are the only drama. Three static latin files come to about 36 KB. Verified: @fontsource/albert-sans, weights 100–900.

styles.navigation: The top bar's anchors (Scan · Records · Reminders · Vet PDF · Privacy · Plans · Questions) become a sticky 48px snow bar after the hero. The current stop is marked by the tennis ball under its link, which rolls between links (transform, 240ms). The lane of prints down the page is the visible route, with each section's H2 set beside its print. On mobile, 'Trail' is a <details> list of the stops, each bulleted with a small inline SVG print, plus Privacy policy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Read the trail'. Every labelled print is a <details> whose summary is the print, the date and the title. Opening one presses the print deeper (its floor shadow darkens over 200ms) and unfolds the record as a note in the snow. The note shows the fields Pawza holds for it, taken from the screenshots (for example 'Annual vaccinations · 7 May 2026 · Rabies, DHPP, Bordetella · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital'), and how it got there: photographed certificate, read on this iPhone, confirmed by you. Dashed future prints open to the reminder (step 5: one gentle nudge before it's due, never a daily nag). As the visitor scrolls, the lane's prints press in one at a time (scale .94→1 with the shadow deepening, 240ms, once each, via IntersectionObserver). Without JS, native <details> works, every print is drawn already pressed, and the 7 May note is open by default. With reduced motion, prints are static and pressed, notes open without animation, and the ball jumps instead of rolling.
styles.motionGrammar: Pressing, not moving. The only motion is depth: prints deepen as they enter view or open, notes unfold (height 200ms), the ball rolls between nav links (240ms), and the sticky bar rises in 180ms. Nothing slides in from the sides and nothing parallaxes. Falling-snow particles are refused outright. With reduced motion, everything is static.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are calm snowfields. A short trail of six small prints walks down the left margin from the top bar's 'Back to Pawza' link to the H1; that is the only world element in the body. The reading column is 68ch, Albert Sans 400 18/1.65 #12232E on #F7F9FB (15:1). H1 is Albert Sans 800 52px and H2s 800 28px. Tables get #E3EAF1 header rows and 1px #A9BACD rules. Alternatives pages set the two 'Choose … if' lists side by side, the FAQ as <details>, and the action row at the end. The privacy page's third-parties section sits on an untrodden band with the transparency.yml facts. Support shows the email in Albert Sans 800 28px and what to include as a list.
styles.assetsNeeded: Two accurate inline SVG print symbols, as a production task: a dog print (four toe pads, heel pad, claw marks) and a cat print (no claws, rounder, three-lobed heel pad), drawn from field-guide references at about 1–2 KB each. Until they exist, a CSS radial-gradient pad cluster stands in. No raster art.
styles.risk: Paw prints are the category's most clichéd motif. Only the field-guide rigour keeps this out of sticker territory: anatomically right pads, claws on the dog and none on the cat, a real trot pattern and dated leader labels. A cold white-and-blue scheme can drift toward the clinical opposite, and a winter scene in July is a seasonal mismatch. The hero proves the scan only through a note, with the screenshot one section down, so it is the weakest of the three at showing 'paper becomes record' above the fold. All trail data is sample data from the screenshots and must stay labelled.
styles.memoryTest: A dog's trail walked across white snow on the page. Every print was a vet record with a date, the dashed prints ahead were reminders, and the privacy part was untouched snow.

canon: The pet-app landing page played straight (never recommended): a smiling dog photo hero with a floating iPhone at right, 'Your pet's whole life, in one place.' over an App Store badge row, paw-print confetti, rounded sans, three paw-icon feature cards, a pricing-card trio and an FAQ accordion.
notes: Dice: key d1586a59, assigned index 4 (the expanding file) → Style A, THE ROLL. --reroll 1 also returned 4 (== N), so I continued: --reroll 2 returned 7 (the literal-reading track candidate) → Style C, SECOND ROLL. Neither roll was 1, so Style B is my #1, the vaccination booklet (IMPECCABLE’S PICK). The roll ran degraded (no catalog challengers, no network), as expected. The candidate order was fixed before rolling. Each signature proves a different leg of the mechanism: A shows filing (paper → read → confirm → behind the right tab), B shows extraction in place (the scrawl becomes typed fields in the same grid), and C shows history and reminders (dated prints, dashed prints ahead) plus privacy as untrodden snow. All three avoid cream-and-serif, even though the app UI itself is cream #EEE9DB with caramel and serif titles; the screenshots sit on white paper (A), pale green pages (B) or snow (C). Owner flags: (1) transparency.yml lists third_party_sdks 1 (ZIPFoundation, local, no network), so the incumbent trust fact '0 third-party SDKs' must not be printed for Pawza. Say 'no ad or analytics SDKs · one local library'. (2) There is no founder block, so there is no founder section or founder Person node; the maker line only, unless the owner adds `founder`. (3) ratings are 5.0 from 1, so no stars. (4) release.last_updated equals first_release (2026-06-06); update it only when an app update actually ships. (5) Every demo value (Bruno, Luna, Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM, Riverside Animal Hospital, the dates and weights) comes from Pawza's own App Store screenshots and must carry a 'sample' label. That data is internally inconsistent (Bruno is '3 yr 6 mo' yet has a 'Puppy vaccination series' in Nov 2025), so prefer other records if that jars. (6) Screenshot 7 names a real vaccine brand; stickers and stamps must use generic names only and must not imitate a real clinic, a manufacturer or the EU pet passport. (7) The six alternatives pages hard-code their copy; the Read variants re-skin them and keep their claims. Fonts verified with npm view and fetched to the board: @fontsource/sofia-sans-extra-condensed, sofia-sans, encode-sans-expanded, encode-sans-condensed, encode-sans, reenie-beanie, albert-sans. Estimated latin font payload: A ≈ 64 KB, B ≈ 108 KB, C ≈ 36 KB. The incumbent head/schema includes (SoftwareApplication + AggregateOffer from schema_price 0 / high 39.99 / count 4, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, HowTo from the 6 steps, speakable on quick_answer) are unchanged in all three.
